cells.tense: Right now you're the one holding both what needs tending and the people who need you, and neither one is dropping.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you've finished to be seen, not just used up — let what you gave be witnessed, and let the ending land as done.
cells.core:
You can carry two needs at once and not crush either one, and that's not luck — that's attention you're actually giving. The people near you feel steadied by it, not managed. When someone comes to you with something heavy, you make room for it without making it about you, and you keep your own footing while you do. The care you hand out arrives as itself, and they take it as itself.

When you finish something, let the finish be a real thing. Hand it to someone you trust and let them say what it cost you. That's not vanity and it's not asking for credit — it's letting the work be complete instead of swallowed, so the next tending starts from full instead of hollow.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing and keep the people close steady while you do.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the bond between you and the people you're close to

cells.tense: You're already planning what comes next before this season has done anything, bracing for the next version of it.
cells.ask: Stop one project a week early and let what's here be enough — the picture in your head isn't a debt anyone owes you yet.
cells.core:
You can see years ahead, and you want the people you love living inside that picture with you. Done cleanly, that long view means they get to be held by someone who's thought about tomorrow and kept it steady for them.

But the vision is running ahead of what's actually here. You're tending an imaginary plot — fixing problems nobody has, providing for a version of them that hasn't shown up — and the people in front of you are getting the manager instead of the companion. Dreams that come from a fully lived life feel different than dreams used to cover the gap. Finish feeling something all the way through, then let the next shape come from that.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a future nobody asked you to carry yet.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the bond between you and the people you're close to

cells.tense: You set this down a while back and you're still standing where you left it, not coming into what's here now.
cells.ask: Pick up one small thing you used to hope for and tend it a little this week — not the whole garden, one plant — and let yourself hope again before you know how it ends.
cells.core:
You care about the people near you and you show it by doing — showing up, holding the practical weight, keeping things alive. When that's flowing, the people close to you can lean on it without having to ask, and you can feel them leaning without it costing you anything.

The doing has gone quiet, though. The love didn't leave, but the believing that it would amount to much isn't in the room with you, and the showing-up has slowed to match. Don't try to force feeling back into a place you've gone still in — that doesn't work and it isn't the way. Go back to hoping, even a little, even about something small, and let the warmth come back on its own once you're actually still in it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped hoping it would grow, so you stopped tending it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the bond between you and the people you're close to

cells.tense: You're already shaping the people around you by how you hold things steady, and you're calling it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person that the care you give is care, not just what's required — let it be named by you, not left for them to guess.
cells.core:
You keep the people close to you steady — you notice what they need, you provide it without being asked, you hold the ground while they find their feet. That's tending, and it's happening every day.

You just don't call it that. You call it doing your job, being practical, keeping things running. And the love that's underneath it stays private, even from you. Name one thing you've done this week as what it actually is, and let the person on the other end know it came from you. That's how it becomes yours out loud instead of a habit nobody — including you — gets to see.
cells.sheetLine: You're already caring for people. You're just calling it keeping things running.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with steady, responsible care
cells.place: in the bond between you and the people you're close to
